newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran's Kish airport ready for wide-bodied aircraft.
newsitem.headline: Iran's Kish airport ready for wide-bodied aircraft.

text.p: Iran's Kish Island airport is ready to receive wide-bodied aircraft after a six billion rial ($2 million) rehabilitation project, the airport director said on Saturday.

"According to the standards set by the International Air Transport Association, the airport can from now receive Boeing 747 and Airbus planes," Iran's state-run news agency IRNA quoted Nosratollah Youssefi as saying.
Kish is one of three free-trade zones on the Gulf set up by Iran in 1989 to draw foreign investment to rebuild its economy after the 1980-88 war with Iraq.
Youssefi said traffic at the airport would increase to 40 flights a day from the current 12.
